_about: Growth engines (stage 3 of the Durand/CAP review). Segment revenue from each company's latest report: 'now' = latest period, 'year_ago' = same period a year earlier ($M). The model splits TTM revenue by the 'now' shares; each segment's year-1 growth = company scenario g1 x (segment growth / company growth), capped at cap_multiple x company g1, then shifted so the revenue-weighted year-1 growth equals the scenario g1 exactly. Every segment fades to the scenario g10 by year 10, then to 2.5% over the advantage period. The company margin is unchanged (one consolidated margin).

AAPL.period: Fiscal year to 26 Sep 2026 vs 27 Sep 2025

Mac.why: Hardware in a mature PC market: part of the ecosystem but not its lock-in.

iPad.why: Flat sales in a mature tablet market.

Wearables, Home and Accessories.why: Flat sales; more competition than iPhone.

AAPL.engines_source: Fiscal 2026 (10-K figures in the Q4 release): gross margin Products 39.3%, Services 76.2%; operating expenses 15.8% of revenue allocated by revenue, so operating margin ~23.5% Products, ~60.4% Services. Apple doesn't report profit by product, so all four product lines share the Products margin.

MSFT.period: Quarter to 30 Sep 2026 (FY27 Q1), year-ago recast from the stated growth (25%, -3%)

Devices and Consumer.why: Windows OEM, Xbox and Surface: mature, cyclical PC and console markets, sales shrinking 3%.

MSFT.engines_source: Microsoft doesn't report operating income by its new segments, so both engines keep the company margin (margin_x 1).

GOOGL.period: Quarter to 30 Sep 2026 vs 30 Sep 2025 (hedging gains excluded)

Google Cloud.why: Third in cloud behind AWS and Azure; returns only recently above the hurdle.

Other Bets.why: Early-stage bets that lose money; no lasting edge yet.

GOOGL.engines_source: Measured Q3 2026 operating margins are Google Services 40.7%, Google Cloud 36.2%, Other Bets -550%, but Cloud carries most of the AI capex, so operating margin overstates its share of cash. Until segment capex is known, all engines keep the company cash margin (margin_x 1).

AWS.why: Top-two cloud platform with a 38% operating margin: a longer edge than retail.

AMZN.engines_source: Measured trailing 12-month operating margins are North America 8.2%, International 3.3%, AWS 37.8%, but AWS also carries most of the capex, so operating margin overstates its share of cash (using it would lift fair value about 47%). Until segment capex is known, all engines keep the company cash margin (margin_x 1).

_engines_about: Per-engine valuation (stage 4, from November 2026): 'engines' gives each segment a margin_x (its operating margin, scaled so today's company margin is unchanged; only the mix moves it) and optionally its own moat class (advantage period and return on new investment; default the company's) with a reason. Rule for adding engines at an earnings review: a reported segment of at least 10% of revenue growing 10+ points faster or slower than the rest.
